summary: Republican Gov. Jim Pillen faces former Democratic state Sen. Lynne Walz of Fremont, and the Washington Sun reports recent polls show Pillen's lead shrinking in a race closer than many Republicans expected. Walz is running on the state budget deficit, property taxes and health cuts while Pillen leans on his tax cut record and conservative groups like the NRA.

issues.why: Walz says the state went from a 1.2 billion dollar surplus to a deficit above 750 million under Pillen, while his campaign touts tax cuts and farm protections.
Walz rejects Pillen's push to fund property tax relief through sales taxes, and her allies suggest changing school aid formulas instead.
Nebraska began enforcing Medicaid work rules in July and more than 1,000 residents have lost coverage, which Walz has targeted.
Diesel above 6 dollars a gallon and higher fertilizer costs are squeezing farmers, and both sides are addressing it.
Pillen backs a stand your ground law while Walz voted against the 2023 constitutional carry law.

storylines.title: Vance rallies with Pillen in North Platte
storylines.what: Vice President JD Vance announced fertilizer manufacturing investment and urged voters to reelect Pillen. Walz answered in a video that your political party does not fix your property tax bill.

storylines.title: Walz holds Siouxland town hall
storylines.what: Walz campaigned in Dakota City on the budget, schools, tax relief and housing, saying she does not care what party voters are from.

storylines.title: Medicaid cuts become a campaign issue
storylines.what: With more than 1,000 Nebraskans off Medicaid under early work requirements, Walz says Pillen's health spending cuts will bring bad outcomes. Republicans point to a federal rural health fund.

storylines.title: NRA backs Pillen at gun range event
storylines.what: The NRA and former Sen. Tom Brewer endorsed Pillen, who said he would support a stand your ground law. Walz called the endorsement another distraction.

storylines.title: Former GOP senators back Walz
storylines.what: Former Republican state Sens. Tim Gragert, Mark Kolterman and John Stinner endorsed Walz. The Pillen campaign called it liberals pretending to be moderates.

storylines.title: Walz platform draws specifics critique
storylines.what: Walz rolled out day one pledges including medical cannabis access and an independent auditor but acknowledged lacking details. Pillen's campaign called her record wrong for Nebraskans.

events.title: Closing the budget hole
events.prompt: The state faces a deficit of more than 750 million dollars after a run of tax cuts. Reporters ask how you would balance the next budget.

opts.label: Pause tax cuts
opts.say: Slow further tax cuts and protect schools and health care.

opts.label: Audit for waste
opts.say: Hire an independent auditor to find waste before any cuts or tax changes.

opts.label: Cut spending more
opts.say: Trim state agencies further and keep taxes on their downward path.

events.title: Property tax relief source
events.prompt: Farmers and homeowners want lower property taxes, and one plan shifts the burden to sales taxes. You must say how you would pay for relief.

opts.label: Rewrite school aid
opts.say: Change the school aid formula so the state carries more of the cost.

opts.label: Targeted farm relief
opts.say: Focus relief on agricultural land while studying broader changes.

opts.label: Shift to sales taxes
opts.say: Expand the sales tax base to cut property taxes across the board.

events.title: Medicaid work rules
events.prompt: Nebraska enforced Medicaid work requirements early and over 1,000 people have lost coverage. Rural hospitals and voters want to know where you stand.

opts.label: Pause enforcement
opts.say: Delay enforcement until the federal start date and restore lost coverage.

opts.label: Fix the paperwork
opts.say: Keep the rules but simplify reporting so eligible workers do not fall off.

opts.label: Defend the rules
opts.say: Stand by work requirements and point to new rural health fund dollars.

events.title: Vance visit response
events.prompt: Vice President Vance comes to North Platte to campaign for the Republican ticket. Your campaign decides how to use the moment.

opts.label: Hit farm costs
opts.say: Point to diesel, fertilizer and grocery prices and say party labels will not fix them.

opts.label: Stay nonpartisan
opts.say: Welcome the fertilizer investment and keep the focus on Nebraska issues.

opts.label: Join the rally
opts.say: Appear with Vance and call for the whole Republican ticket to win.

regions.name: Omaha metro
regions.note: The state's largest population center, with a competitive Omaha core and Republican leaning suburbs.

regions.name: Lincoln
regions.note: The capital and university city leans Democratic, surrounded by Republican farm counties.

regions.name: Northeast Nebraska
regions.note: Heavily Republican farm and meatpacking country, with Walz's Fremont base and a Latino community in Dakota County.

regions.name: Central Nebraska
regions.note: Republican Tri Cities and Platte Valley towns where farm costs dominate.

regions.name: Panhandle and Sandhills
regions.note: Sparse ranch country that is among the most Republican in the nation.
